THE WIRE SHAPE WAS READ FROM THE SPEC, NOT GUESSED. modelcontextprotocol.io/seps/2322-MRTR: the server answers with result { resultType: 'input_required', inputRequests: { <key>: { method: 'elicitation/create', params: { mode, message, requestedSchema } } }, requestState }, and the client re-issues the SAME tools/call with params.inputResponses[<key>] = an ElicitResult { action, content } plus the echoed requestState. A conformance test pins every one of those field names, because this is one of the few places where being subtly wrong produces NO error at all - a client that does not recognise the shape either ignores the prompt or reports the tool as broken, and neither says which. FOUR PROBES AGAINST A LIVE STACK, all four as designed. (1) Modern client, publish with mode=confirm and no answer yet: InputRequiredResult, 'Put this item live on eBay now?'. (2) Retry with action=accept and confirm=false: 'The seller said no, so nothing was changed. Do not try again unless they ask for it.' (3) Retry with confirm=true: passes THROUGH to the handler, which then rejects the fake confirm token - which is the proof that elicitation does not replace the token. (4) A legacy 2025-11-25 client making the same call gets no prompt at all and goes straight to the handler's token check. ACCEPT WITH confirm:false IS A REFUSAL, and that is the case most likely to be got wrong: a completed form reads as consent if you only check `action === 'accept'`. Decline and cancel are refusals too, worded differently ('dismissed' rather than 'said no'), and all three tell the model NOT to try again - a model retrying a refusal has done the one thing the prompt existed to prevent. IT SITS AFTER THE GATES AND BEFORE THE HANDLER. There is no point asking a person to approve something the plan, the scope or the budget was going to refuse, and asking after the publish is not asking. A source guard asserts both orderings by index, plus the modern-era condition. PREVIEWS DO NOT PROMPT. humanConfirmation returns null unless mode is 'confirm' (reprice apply always asks - it has no preview mode). A prompt for something that changes nothing is a prompt a seller learns to dismiss, and the next one is the publish. Bulk questions carry the COUNT, because a number is the one part a seller can check at a glance. A test asserts every prompting tool ALSO takes a confirm_token, so the pair can never drift apart: elicitation asks a person, the token proves the payload did not change between the question and the action.
acceptanceCriteria: A tool may declare that it wants human confirmation. The dispatcher, not the handler, turns that into an InputRequiredResult with inputRequests on clients advertising the 2026-07-28 revision.
A client that retries with inputResponses reaches the handler with the human's answer available; a client that does not support it gets the current two-call flow unchanged.
The confirm token is still required in both paths. Elicitation must not become a way to publish without one.
A declined elicitation is a refusal, not a timeout: the tool reports that the seller said no and changes nothing.
Legacy-era clients (2025-11-25 and earlier) are unaffected - they never see an InputRequiredResult.
Conformance: the InputRequiredResult shape is pinned in mcp-conformance_test.ts, because it is a wire contract.

userStories.title: Write tools: reprice - preview then apply, single and bulk
userStories.description: As a seller, I want to reprice from the chat with the same preview I get in the dashboard, so that I can move stale inventory without opening the app.
acceptanceCriteria: `gradethread_reprice_preview` wraps POST /api/flipdesk/pricing/reprice/preview and returns the per-listing before/after with the rule or comp basis for each.
`gradethread_reprice_apply` wraps POST /api/flipdesk/pricing/reprice/apply and requires a confirm_token from the preview, using the shared confirm lib from US-9116.
`gradethread_price_suggestions` wraps GET /api/flipdesk/pricing/suggestions, and apply/dismiss wrap the existing /suggestions/:id/apply and /dismiss endpoints.

A price change larger than a configurable percentage (suggest 25%) or crossing below a stored floor/cost basis is refused at apply time with the reason, even WITH a valid token. A confirmation is not a safety net for an arithmetic error.
Bulk apply is capped per call and per hour by US-9119's budget, and the preview always states how many listings will change before the token is issued.
Annotated destructiveHint:true. Audit rows record the listing ids and both prices.
userStories.notes: flipdesk-pricing.ts already has preview/apply, rules and suggestions - this story is adapters plus the floor guard, not new pricing logic. [DONE 2026-08-19] Shipped: services/edge-functions/src/lib/mcp-reprice-tools.ts (five tools), lib/reprice-port.ts and lib/api-pricing.ts. Tests: src/tests/mcp-reprice-tools_test.ts 20 passed, full edge suite 7518 passed / 0 failed, tenant-isolation lane against a live local stack 219 passed / 0 failed with five new cross-tenant cases. THE FOUR PRICING BODIES ARE NOW FUNCTIONS the HTTP handlers call: applyPriceSuggestion, dismissPriceSuggestion, previewRepriceFor and applyRepriceFor, sliced verbatim out of the handlers with only the context reads and response builders rewritten. The route registers them into lib/reprice-port.ts, so a tool and the dashboard cannot price a listing differently. The eBay-FIRST order (US-467) survives the move and is called out in both the port and the extracted function: a local write after a failed remote update leaves the seller's price disagreeing with the live listing and nothing surfaces it. AC4 IS THE POINT OF THIS STORY AND IT IS WHAT THE TESTS ARE ABOUT. A confirm token proves the seller saw these numbers and that they have not moved. It does NOT prove the numbers were right. A model that computes a 90% drop, shows it, gets a yes and applies it has satisfied the entire protocol and the seller has still lost the money. So apply refuses a move over 25% or a price below the item's cost floor EVEN WITH a valid token, names the listing and the percentage, and says the confirmation does not change that. The 24% case is tested from the other side so the guard is not simply refusing everything. THE GUARD READS THE CURRENT PRICE, NOT ONE THE CALLER SUPPLIED, which has its own test: a caller declaring its own 'current price' could make any move look small, so the percentage is computed against a fresh preview and the only number the caller controls is the target. AC5: THE COUNT IS STATED BEFORE THE TOKEN IS ISSUED. 'Reprice your listings' and 'change the price on 34 listings' are different things to say yes to. A preview with nothing to change issues NO token, because a token over an empty change set invites a confirm that does nothing and reports success. REPORTING: a failed row carries the marketplace's own reason and says both sides kept the old price, so a seller does not go looking for a mismatch that is not there. Applying one suggestion reports whether eBay was ACTUALLY pushed rather than assuming - 'applied' with ebay_synced false on a live listing would be a lie, and the underlying path deliberately leaves the suggestion pending in that case so it stays retryable. SCOPES: preview and the suggestions list are read-scoped and write nothing; both carry openWorldHint because they call eBay Browse for comparables, so the answer moves between calls. Apply and the two per-suggestion verbs are submit-scoped and destructive. Dismiss is on the price_change budget despite changing no price, because the coverage guard requires every destructive tool to be budgeted and a loop dismissing every suggestion a seller has is worth stopping. One isolation shape worth recording: reprice preview is a per-listing REPORT, so a foreign id correctly comes back as an empty item list rather than as an error - loadOwnedRepriceListings filters on inventory_items.user_id and the row never enters the set. The assertion is therefore assertListExcludes plus 'no token issued', not assertToolDeniedById.

userStories.title: Write tools: end, delist and relist - confirm-gated
userStories.description: As a seller, I want to end or relist items from the chat, so that the last manual step in the pipeline is covered.
acceptanceCriteria: `gradethread_end_listing` wraps POST /api/flipdesk/listings/:id/end and requires a confirm_token naming the specific listing.
`gradethread_relist` reuses the existing relist path, including the auto-relist rules already in the product, and reports the NEW listing id.
Bulk end is exposed only behind a preview that lists every affected item by title, and a token bound to that exact set. A count is not a preview.
The lifecycle-verb rule from US-9116 applies: end and relist must confirm the marketplace result rather than infer success from a non-error response.

Ending a listing with an active offer, a pending order, or a cancelled-order zero-quantity state is refused with the specific reason - the zero-quantity case is already handled elsewhere in the product and must not regress here.
Annotated destructiveHint:true. Audit rows written.
userStories.notes: This is the most dangerous tool in the set and the one an injected instruction would most want to reach. It ships after US-9111 (untrusted wrapping) and US-9113 (audit) for that reason. [DONE 2026-08-19] Shipped: services/edge-functions/src/lib/mcp-lifecycle-tools.ts - gradethread_end_listing, gradethread_end_listings and gradethread_relist, all confirm-gated. Tests: src/tests/mcp-lifecycle-tools_test.ts 13 passed, full edge suite 7551 passed / 0 failed, tenant-isolation lane against a live local stack 222 passed / 0 failed with three new cross-tenant cases and both controls checked by hand (A previewing A's own listing gets the title, price and a token; B gets 'None of those listings are in this workspace'). BULK END LOOPS THE SINGLE END. endOwnedListing is the one implementation of 'end this listing' - it dispatches on the same planner the sale-triggered auto-end uses, queues the no-API marketplaces for the Lister extension, and marks the local row ended only when the listing is genuinely not live. The bulk tool calls it once per listing rather than adding a THIRD adapter.delist loop to a codebase that already has two, and a test asserts no delist call site appeared in the connector tools. QUEUED IS NOT COUNTED AS ENDED, which is the US-2641 shape applied to this verb. A Poshmark or Mercari listing has no delist API: it is stamped for the extension and STAYS LIVE until the seller next opens FlipDesk. The tool reports ENDED, QUEUED, ALREADY ENDED and STILL LIVE as four different things and counts queued in the still-live total. Collapsing them into 'ended' is how a seller believes a buyer can no longer buy an item that is still for sale. A COUNT IS NOT A PREVIEW (AC3). Bulk preview lists every affected item by title, marketplace, status and current price, and the token is bound to that exact SET - and specifically to what is CURRENTLY ownable rather than to the ids that were asked for, so a listing that leaves the workspace between preview and confirm invalidates the token instead of being silently dropped. RELIST NEEDED ONE EXTRACTION AND ONE NEW PLAN-GATE FUNCTION. The relist handler body became relistOwnedListing in flipdesk-ebay.ts, registered through lib/ebay-publish-port.ts. It is a separate port function rather than publish({relist:true}) because the route does real work around that call: it refuses eBay-ORIGINATED listings, checks the active-listing cap, and replenishes the quantity BEFORE publishing so the publish context resolves a non-zero availableQuantity - calling publish directly would relist at quantity zero. The capacity gate needed a Hono context, so lib/plan-gate.ts gained capacityAllowedForUser, the sibling of featureAllowedForUser: same plan resolution, same numbers, fails CLOSED, and it exists so a tool cannot be the one entry point that skips the active-listing cap. THE RELIST TOKEN COVERS THE QUANTITY, not just the listing. Relisting one and relisting twelve are different decisions and the seller agreed to one of them. And a relist returning no NEW listing id is reported as unconfirmed rather than as success, with why not to simply try again (a duplicate). AC2's 'reports the NEW listing id' and AC4's 'confirm rather than infer' are the same requirement from two sides. AC5 IS SATISFIED BY DELEGATION, deliberately. Active offers, pending orders and the cancelled-order zero-quantity state are handled inside endOwnedListing and the paths beneath it; the tool adds no second opinion, so there is nothing here that can regress them. Bulk end applies the same bulkActions plan gate the dashboard's bulk-end applies, through featureAllowedForUser, and the refusal names the single-listing tool so a model does not just retry. Both end tools and relist share the end_listing budget: the cap is about how many of a seller's listings a model may take off sale per hour, and doing it in one call does not make it fewer. ⚠ NOTE FOR WHOEVER READS THIS NEXT: a second agent was editing the same tree during this story (mcp-audit.ts, routes/mcp.ts and an auditDetail field on McpToolResult, which is US-9117 AC6's audit-row work). Only this story's files were staged. mcp-tools.ts carries that agent's auditDetail field because git stages whole files - it is an optional interface field nobody sets yet, so it is inert on its own.

userStories.title: Per-session and per-day action budgets for connector writes
userStories.description: As a seller, I want a hard ceiling on what a single conversation can do, so that a runaway loop costs me one bad hour instead of my whole store.
acceptanceCriteria: Configurable caps enforced server-side, per API key and per rolling window: publishes per hour, price changes per hour, ends per hour, grades per day, and AI-spend cents per day. Defaults are conservative and stated in the vault note from US-9101.
Caps come from the plan decision in US-9101 - whether they share FLIPDESK_PLANS.aiActionsPerMonth or use their own counter is settled there, not re-decided here.
Hitting a cap returns a JSON-RPC error naming the cap, the window and when it resets, so the model tells the seller something true rather than retrying.
Caps are enforced in the tool dispatcher, not in each handler. A per-handler cap is a cap that the next tool forgets.
The counter store failing CLOSES the write path (matching the fail-closed choice already made for /api/v1 rate limits) while leaving read tools working.
A seller-visible view of today's connector usage exists - extend the existing API-key usage surface (src/pages/api-keys.tsx) rather than building a new page.
Tests cover: cap reached, cap reset at the window boundary, counter-store outage closes writes and leaves reads open.
userStories.notes: This is what makes the write tools defensible in a support conversation. Without it, 'the AI did it' has no ceiling attached. [DONE 2026-08-18] Shipped: services/edge-functions/src/lib/mcp-budget.ts plus the check in the dispatcher. Tests: src/tests/mcp-budget_test.ts, 11 passed / 0 failed, with the two properties that matter sabotage-verified (making the counter outage return 0 instead of refusing breaks the fail-closed test; adding a destructive tool with no budget breaks the mapping guard). BUILT BEFORE THE WRITE TOOLS ON PURPOSE, which is the order the plan wanted. A cap added after the tools it caps is a cap that was absent for however long that took. WHAT THIS CATCHES THAT RATE LIMITS DO NOT. US-9105's limits stop a flood. They do not stop a well-paced mistake: forty publishes over forty minutes sits inside every per-minute budget and is still a seller's whole store live at the wrong price. The budgets are per-hour and per-day, per credential. ENFORCED IN THE DISPATCHER via budgetKindForTool(name), not per handler - a per-handler cap is the one the next tool forgets, and the next tool is the one nobody reviewed as carefully. A test enumerates the registry and FAILS if any tool annotated destructiveHint spends from no budget, so the mapping cannot fall behind. FAIL CLOSED ON WRITES, and the counter THROWS rather than returning 0 so the policy is the caller's to state: if we cannot read how much has been spent, 'unknown' must not read as 'none' for an action that ends listings. checkBudget itself never throws, so a handler's try/catch cannot turn an outage into a retry. Reads are untouched - refusing to answer 'what is in my inventory' during a counter outage helps nobody. THE COUNTER READS THE AUDIT LOG (US-9113) rather than a new table. A separate counter table would be a second record of the same events, and the two would disagree the first time one of them failed to write. The numbers are conservative and live in ONE table (DEFAULT_BUDGETS): 20 publishes/hour, 50 price changes/hour, 20 ends/hour, 200 grades/day, 2000 cents of AI spend/day. US-9101 decides whether they vary by plan; until then one table applies to everyone and it is the tight one. A refusal names the number, the window, when it resets, and tells the seller to use the dashboard if it cannot wait.

userStories.title: OAuth 2.1: protected-resource metadata, AS metadata, and Client ID Metadata Documents
userStories.description: As a seller, I want to add GradeThread in claude.ai by pasting a URL and signing in, so that I do not have to generate and paste an API key.
acceptanceCriteria: GET /.well-known/oauth-protected-resource (RFC 9728) served from the edge service, naming the authorization server and the resource identifier for /mcp. This is a MUST for an MCP server; clients use it for authorization-server discovery.

GET /.well-known/oauth-authorization-server (RFC 8414) advertising the authorize, token and revocation endpoints, PKCE S256 (plain is rejected), grant types (authorization_code, refresh_token), scopes_supported, and authorization_response_iss_parameter_supported: true. OpenID Connect Discovery is the permitted alternative; we implement RFC 8414.

CLIENT ID METADATA DOCUMENTS ARE THE PRIMARY REGISTRATION PATH, not dynamic registration. The AS accepts an HTTPS URL as client_id, fetches the client metadata document from it, and validates the declared redirect_uris. RFC 7591 Dynamic Client Registration is DEPRECATED in the MCP authorization spec and is retained here only as a fallback for clients that cannot use metadata documents.
If the DCR fallback is implemented, POST /oauth/register is rate-limited and fail-closed. An open registration endpoint is an open write endpoint.

Redirect URIs are validated at registration AND again at authorize. Exact match and https only, with ONE exemption: loopback. Claude Code redirects to localhost and 127.0.0.1 on a VARYING PORT, so loopback matching must ignore the port; every other host is exact-match. https://claude.ai/api/mcp/auth_callback must be accepted for hosted Claude surfaces. No wildcards, no open redirects.

scopes_supported represents the minimal set needed for basic functionality; broader permissions are requested incrementally through the step-up flow driven by the 403 insufficient_scope challenge from US-9104. offline_access is NOT listed in scopes_supported or in any WWW-Authenticate challenge - refresh tokens are not a resource requirement.
An unauthenticated request to /mcp returns 401 with WWW-Authenticate pointing at the protected-resource metadata, which is how an MCP client discovers where to log in.
userStories.notes: [REWRITTEN 2026-08-18 after US-9102] The original story made RFC 7591 dynamic client registration the primary mechanism. It is deprecated. Client ID Metadata Documents (draft-ietf-oauth-client-id-metadata-document-00) are the replacement and both servers and clients SHOULD support them. The loopback port-agnostic rule is what makes Claude Code work at all - exact-string redirect matching rejects it every time. GradeThread has never been an OAuth authorization SERVER; the eBay and Google integrations make us a client. This is genuinely new surface, which is why it sits after the tools rather than before them. [PARTIAL 2026-08-18] SHIPPED: services/edge-functions/src/lib/oauth-metadata.ts (both discovery documents, the redirect-URI rules, and the resource identifier), mounted in main.ts, with the 401 challenge pointing at the real document. Tests: src/tests/oauth-metadata_test.ts, 21 passed / 0 failed. THE DOCUMENTS ARE NOT SERVED YET, and that is the decision worth recording. Publishing RFC 9728 and RFC 8414 metadata before /oauth/authorize and /oauth/token exist would make the connector broken in a NEW way: a client reads the metadata, starts an authorization flow, and 404s at the authorize endpoint. TODAY the same client sees no discovery, falls back to a static credential, and works. Advertising a capability we do not have takes the working path away too. So both routes 404 and the challenge omits resource_metadata unless MCP_OAUTH_ENABLED is set; the flag flips on in the same change that lands the endpoints. Verified live with the flag off: both documents 404 and the challenge is `Bearer scope="read submit"` with no dead pointer. The documents themselves are complete regardless of the flag, and a test says so - anything the flag also gated would be untested until the day it flipped. THE REDIRECT RULE IS THE PART THAT DECIDES WHETHER CLAUDE CODE CAN CONNECT AT ALL. It redirects to http://localhost:<port> with a port chosen at run time, so exact-string matching rejects it every single time and the failure reads as 'the connector cannot be added from a terminal'. OAuth 2.1 permits loopback with a variable port for exactly this reason. The exemption is scoped to the PORT and to loopback hosts: the path still has to match (a registered /callback must not accept /steal), a fragment is refused because it smuggles a second destination, and every non-loopback host is compared whole - so claude.ai.evil.com and a /extra suffix are both refused. Each of those is a test. STILL TO DO, all needing the oauth_clients table and therefore the US-9122 migration: POST /oauth/register (the DEPRECATED DCR fallback), and Client ID Metadata Document fetching at authorize time, which is the path the spec now prefers. The metadata already advertises client_id_metadata_document_supported: true, which is why the flag matters - it is advertised but not yet honoured. [DONE 2026-08-18] Shipped: services/edge-functions/src/lib/oauth-clients.ts (Client ID Metadata Document resolution) and POST /oauth/register in src/routes/oauth.ts. Tests: src/tests/oauth-clients_test.ts 16 passed, src/tests/oauth-register_test.ts 10 passed, full edge suite 7445 passed / 0 failed. THE FEATURE IS SSRF WITH A SPECIFICATION ATTACHED. A Client ID Metadata Document means the client_id IS an https URL and we fetch it from inside our network, on the word of whoever is calling. Every fetch goes through lib/ssrf.ts safeFetch, which resolves the host, refuses private and link-local addresses, and connects to the IP it cleared rather than re-resolving, so DNS cannot change its answer between the check and the connection. Capped at 64KB with a 5s timeout and at most 2 redirects. Two tests hand the REAL guard a hostile URL (127.0.0.1 and 169.254.169.254, the cloud instance-metadata address) rather than trusting a stub. THREE SMALLER RULES THAT EACH CLOSE A HOLE. (1) A document declaring a different client_id than the URL it came from is refused, or a document at one URL asserts redirect URIs on behalf of another client and the URL stops meaning anything. (2) Content-type is checked BEFORE parsing, because a 40KB HTML error page is not a metadata document and parsing one spends effort on the only thing the caller controls. (3) A non-https client_id is treated as opaque and looked up, never fetched, so http://internal-service/ cannot become a fetch of an internal service. A METADATA CLIENT IS RE-FETCHED, NOT CACHED FOREVER. The row exists so the grant and code foreign keys have something to point at; it is upserted on every resolve. A stale cached copy is a redirect allowlist nobody is maintaining. REDIRECT VALIDATION IS THE SAME ON BOTH PATHS - metadata document and POST /oauth/register both go through invalidRedirectUris. A client that arrives by URL must not get a laxer redirect check than one that arrives by POST; that difference is the hole someone finds. The loopback port-agnostic rule holds on both, which is what lets a connector be added from a terminal at all. REGISTER ISSUES NO CLIENT SECRET and accepts at most ten redirect_uris. An open registration endpoint is an open write endpoint: a public client using PKCE does not need a secret, and a secret handed to an anonymous registrant is a credential with nobody accountable for it. RESOLVECLIENT HAS NO CALLER YET and that is the residual risk, because the authorize endpoint is US-9121. A guard test in oauth-clients_test.ts scans routes/oauth.ts and fails if an /authorize handler ever appears without importing lib/oauth-clients.ts - an authorize handler that reads client_id straight off the query string accepts any client_id anyone sends and looks like a working flow while doing it. The guard was verified by pointing it at /register, where it failed as intended.

userStories.title: OAuth 2.1: authorize endpoint and the consent screen on gradethread.com
userStories.description: As a seller, I want to see exactly what I am granting before I grant it, so that connecting Claude is an informed decision.
acceptanceCriteria: GET /oauth/authorize validates client_id, redirect_uri, response_type=code, PKCE code_challenge (S256) and the requested scopes, then redirects to a consent page on gradethread.com.

A new frontend route (suggest /connect/claude) renders the consent screen: which client is asking, which scopes, what each scope allows in plain language ('read your inventory and grades', 'create and publish listings', 'change prices and end listings'), and the workspace the grant applies to.
The seller must be signed in with the existing Supabase PKCE session; an unauthenticated visit routes through the normal login and returns to consent afterwards with the request intact.
Scopes are individually declinable where that is meaningful - a seller who wants read-only must be able to get read-only from the consent screen, not only from the API-keys page.
Approving issues a single-use authorization code bound to the client, the redirect_uri, the code_challenge and the granted scopes, with a short TTL (<= 60s per OAuth 2.1 guidance).
Denying returns the spec's error redirect, never a dead end.

The consent page is registered per the SEO route rules ONLY if it should be indexable - it should not be; confirm it is excluded from PUBLIC_ROUTES and the prerender entry rather than accidentally included.
The page passes npm run ui:check with zero findings in src/ and follows the brand rules - no gradient text, no colored side tab, no nested cards.
userStories.notes: The consent screen is the highest-trust page in the product. It is the one place a seller decides whether an AI can spend their money. [BLOCKED 2026-08-18] Needs the consent screen in the React app (a new route under src/), which is where the concurrent SEO agent is working - and needs the authorize endpoint from US-9122, which needs its migration. Not started rather than half-started: a consent screen is the highest-trust page in the product, the one place a seller decides whether an AI can spend their money, and it is not a page to build against an endpoint that does not exist yet. [DONE 2026-08-19, unblocked once 00620 was applied] Shipped: services/edge-functions/src/lib/oauth-authorize.ts, GET /oauth/authorize and POST /api/oauth/consent in routes/oauth.ts, and src/pages/connect-claude.tsx at /connect/claude. Tests: src/tests/oauth-authorize_test.ts 22 passed, full edge suite 7624 passed / 0 failed, frontend tsc + eslint clean, npm run ui:check 0 blocking in src/, and the route/SEO guard suites 40 passed. THE OPEN-REDIRECTOR LINE IS WHAT SHAPES THE ENDPOINT. There are two kinds of invalid request and they must be answered differently. A bad client_id or a redirect_uri the client never registered is FATAL and is answered on our own origin - redirecting an error to an unverified address is what turns an authorization endpoint into an open redirector, and hands the attacker whatever the query string carried. Everything else (bad response_type, missing PKCE, unknown scope, wrong resource) redirects to the VERIFIED uri with error=, because by then we know where the client lives. validateAuthorizeRequest returns three arms rather than a boolean for exactly this reason, and most of the test file is about which side of that line each failure falls on. AN UNKNOWN CLIENT DOES NOT SAY WHETHER IT WAS UNKNOWN OR UNREACHABLE. Saying which tells someone probing client ids whether they guessed a real one; the reason goes to the log. THE CONSENT PAGE IS NOT TRUSTED. GET /oauth/authorize validates and then redirects to /connect/claude carrying the request in the query string; nothing is stored, because nothing has been agreed. Approving posts back to /api/oauth/consent, which RE-VALIDATES every parameter through the same function - the page is a browser page and its parameters are exactly as untrusted as the ones that arrived first. Narrowing scopes there is the point (AC4); widening them or swapping the redirect is refused by the code that refused it the first time. THE GRANT IS WRITTEN AGAINST THE SESSION USER, never a body field. /api/oauth/consent is mounted under authMiddleware; a consent endpoint that took a user id from its caller would let anyone mint a grant for anyone. SCOPES NARROW, NEVER WIDEN, and both directions are tested. The requested set is the ceiling: a consent page that could add a scope is a consent page that could grant itself one. Granting nothing is refused rather than stored as an empty grant. RFC 9207 iss GOES ON ERROR REDIRECTS TOO. Only sending it on success is how a mixed-up-provider attack survives - a client cannot confirm which authorization server answered. CODE TTL IS 60 SECONDS (AC5), stored hashed, carrying the challenge, the redirect_uri and the resource so the token endpoint can re-check all three rather than trust the exchange. A test asserts the plaintext code does not appear in the stored row. DENYING IS NOT A DEAD END (AC6): it returns the spec's access_denied redirect, so Claude says 'connection cancelled' rather than hanging on a page that went nowhere. THE PAGE IS WRITTEN FOR SOMEONE WHO HAS NEVER HEARD THE WORD SCOPE. Each permission is stated as what it lets the AI DO and what that COSTS - 'Grade items, write listings and change prices ... this spends your grading credits and changes what buyers see and pay' rather than 'grants write access'. The client is identified by the HOST of its client_id URL, never by a name it chose for itself, because a self-declared display name is not evidence. Read is marked required (the connection does nothing without it); everything else is a switch a seller can turn off and still connect. AC3 needed no new code: ProtectedRoute already preserves pathname AND search into ?next=, so an unauthenticated visit routes through login and returns with the request intact. The page sits inside ProtectedRoute but OUTSIDE DashboardLayout - a sidebar on a decision this size is an invitation to click something else. AC7 CONFIRMED BY ABSENCE: /connect/claude is NOT in PUBLIC_ROUTES and NOT in the prerender entry, and the route/SEO guard suites pass. It only means anything with a live authorization request in its query string, so an indexed copy would be a permanently broken search result. One guard needed following: oauth-clients_test.ts's 'an /authorize endpoint must resolve its client' fired the moment /authorize existed, because resolution moved one level down (route to validateAuthorizeRequest to resolveClient). It now follows the CHAIN and checks both links, so a route that stops validating and a validator that stops resolving each still fail it.

userStories.title: OAuth 2.1: token, refresh and revocation, with the storage migration
userStories.description: As the operator, I want issued grants to be revocable and short-lived, so that a compromised client is a bounded incident.
acceptanceCriteria: POST /oauth/token implements authorization_code (with PKCE S256 verification) and refresh_token grants, and MUST accept application/x-www-form-urlencoded request bodies - Anthropic's connector review checks for exactly this. Access tokens are short-lived (suggest 1 hour); refresh tokens rotate on every use and the old one is invalidated.

RFC 8707 RESOURCE INDICATORS ARE ENFORCED. The authorize and token requests carry a `resource` parameter naming the canonical MCP server URI (https://functions.gradethread.com/mcp), the issued token is audience-bound to it, and /mcp MUST validate that an incoming token was issued for us as the audience. A token minted for another resource MUST be rejected. This is the confused-deputy defence and it is a spec MUST, not a nicety.
Authorization responses include the `iss` parameter (RFC 9207), including on error responses, matching the authorization_response_iss_parameter_supported: true advertised in US-9120's metadata.
Refresh-token reuse detection: presenting an already-rotated refresh token revokes the whole grant chain and logs a security event. Rotation without reuse detection is bookkeeping, not security.
POST /oauth/revoke (RFC 7009) revokes a token or a whole grant.

A new migration (next free number) creates oauth_clients, oauth_authorization_codes and oauth_grants/tokens with the token values STORED HASHED, never in plaintext - same posture as api_keys (HMAC with pepper where configured). Indexes on the lookup paths; expired rows swept by a job.
US-1108 triple: idempotent SQL, EXPECTED_SCHEMA_VERSION bumped in the same commit, self-record footer. HELD - added to PENDING_MIGRATIONS.md and not pushed until the operator applies it.
All three tables registered in rls-guard_test.ts as service-role-only.
The seller can see and revoke connected clients from the account UI - extend the existing API-keys page rather than adding a parallel surface.

/mcp accepts an OAuth access token in Authorization: Bearer alongside the API key path from US-9104, resolving to the same tenant context. The token's granted scopes gate tools/list and tools/call exactly as key scopes do, and scope hierarchies are honoured (a broader scope satisfies a narrower one).
userStories.notes: [UPDATED 2026-08-18 after US-9102] Added the RFC 8707 audience-binding MUST, the RFC 9207 iss requirement and the form-urlencoded token endpoint - all three are spec or review requirements the original story did not name. Load the migrations skill. Two migrations now exist in this epic (US-9113 and this one); check the apply order and the numbers against the live 00618 baseline before writing either. [NOT STARTED 2026-08-18] The discovery documents it completes are built and tested (US-9120) and deliberately not served until this lands. What remains here is genuinely security-critical and self-contained: authorization codes with PKCE S256 verification, token rotation with reuse detection, RFC 8707 audience binding, RFC 7009 revocation, and the oauth_clients / oauth_authorization_codes / oauth_grants tables - a SECOND held migration. Sequenced after US-9121 rather than before it because a token endpoint with no authorize endpoint and no consent screen cannot be exercised end to end, and 'it compiles' is not verification for this one. [PARTIAL 2026-08-18] SHIPPED: services/edge-functions/src/lib/oauth-tokens.ts - PKCE S256 verification, single-use authorization codes, refresh rotation with reuse detection, opaque token generation, hashed-at-rest storage and RFC 8707 audience binding. Tests: src/tests/oauth-tokens_test.ts, 25 passed / 0 failed. Every case corresponds to an ATTACK rather than a happy path, which is deliberate: an OAuth implementation that passes the happy path and nothing else is the normal way these ship broken, because the happy path is the one part everyone exercises by hand. THREE DEFENCES SABOTAGE-VERIFIED. Accepting `plain` PKCE fails its test. Detecting a replayed authorization code but leaving the grant alive fails its test. Rotating refresh tokens without revoking the chain fails its test. Each of those is a real implementation that would look correct in review. FOUR RULES WORTH RECORDING, because each is a decision rather than a transcription. (1) A REPLAYED CODE REVOKES THE GRANT IT PRODUCED. A code presented twice means the client is broken or someone else has it, and from here those are indistinguishable - so the safe reading is the second one. Detecting the replay while leaving the grant alive is not a defence: the grant is the thing the attacker wanted. (2) A CODE THAT FAILS A LATER CHECK IS STILL SPENT. Otherwise the failure reasons are an oracle a caller retries against, varying one parameter at a time, until something lines up. Same reasoning as the confirm token in US-9116. (3) ROTATION WITHOUT REUSE DETECTION IS BOOKKEEPING. Issuing a new token each time only helps if presenting an OLD one is treated as evidence a copy exists elsewhere. When it happens the whole chain dies - the legitimate client re-authorizes, which is cheap, and the attacker's copy dies with it, which is the point. A test asserts the NEW token stops working too, not just the replayed one. (4) AUDIENCE IS COMPARED EXACTLY. Trailing-slash and case leniency is what turns an audience check into a prefix check, and the whole reason the check exists is the confused deputy: a token a seller granted to another service on the same authorization server must not be accepted here. The store is an injected interface, which is why all of this could be built and reviewed BEFORE the migration exists. What remains: the oauth_clients / oauth_authorization_codes / oauth_grants tables (a second held migration), the /oauth/token, /oauth/revoke and /oauth/register endpoints, and flipping MCP_OAUTH_ENABLED so the US-9120 discovery documents start being served. [STORAGE LAYER DONE 2026-08-18] Shipped: supabase/migrations/00620_oauth_authorization_server.sql (oauth_clients, oauth_grants, oauth_authorization_codes, oauth_refresh_tokens plus sweep_oauth_expired), EXPECTED_SCHEMA_VERSION bumped to 00620 in the same commit, manifest regenerated, all four tables registered in SERVICE_ROLE_ONLY, and services/edge-functions/src/lib/oauth-store.ts implementing the TokenStore over them. Tests: src/tests/oauth-store_test.ts, 4 passed / 0 failed AGAINST THE REAL DATABASE - the rules are covered by the fake store in oauth-tokens_test.ts, so this file only asserts what only Postgres can be wrong about. MIGRATION HELD. TWO are now outstanding: apply 00619 then 00620, both before the next edge deploy, or the boot guard refuses to start on a database at 00618. PENDING_MIGRATIONS.md leads with that. NO REVOKE in the file, for the reason 00527 is permanently blocked (US-2403); sweep_oauth_expired guards in its body and was verified on the live stack raising 42501 for anon. TWO ORDERING DECISIONS THE STORE MAKES, both of which only a real database can get wrong. (1) markCodeConsumed updates conditionally on consumed_at IS NULL, so two requests racing the same code cannot both believe they were first. (2) rotateRefresh MARKS THE OLD TOKEN BEFORE inserting the new one: if the insert went first and the mark then failed, two live refresh tokens would exist in a rotating scheme, which is the exact state rotation prevents. Marking first means the worst case is a grant with no usable refresh token, costing the seller a re-authorization instead of costing them the grant's security. A test asserts the outcome - old row marked, new row not pre-marked, generation 2. revokeGrant records a REASON ('user', 'reuse_detected', 'code_replayed', 'admin'). After the fact there is no way to tell a seller's own disconnect from a token that turned up twice, and those are different conversations. STILL TO DO: the /oauth/token, /oauth/revoke and /oauth/register endpoints, which are thin over this layer, and flipping MCP_OAUTH_ENABLED. The authorize endpoint and consent screen stay with US-9121. [ENDPOINTS DONE 2026-08-18] Shipped: services/edge-functions/src/routes/oauth.ts - POST /oauth/token (authorization_code and refresh_token grants) and POST /oauth/revoke (RFC 7009), mounted public and gated on MCP_OAUTH_ENABLED. Tests: src/tests/oauth-endpoints_test.ts, 10 passed / 0 failed AGAINST THE REAL DATABASE. MIGRATION 00620 WAS AMENDED rather than followed by a 00621: it had no access-token storage and the token endpoint needs one. 00620 is applied nowhere but the local stack and PENDING_MIGRATIONS.md still lists it as pending, so amending is legitimate - and a 00621 whose only reason for existing is that I forgot a table is worse for whoever reads the directory in a year, because it implies two decisions where there was one. Five tables now; the note and the rls-guard registration were updated to match. ACCESS TOKENS ARE OPAQUE AND STORED, not signed and stateless. A signed token would save the table and save nothing else: every request loads the grant anyway, to learn the tenant and the scopes and to check the grant is not revoked. Stateless buys no read, costs a signing-key rotation story, and turns 'revoke this now' into 'revoke this within the token lifetime'. THE TWO WAYS AN ENDPOINT UNDOES A CORRECT RULE UNDERNEATH IT, both tested. (1) SAYING WHY. Every authorization-code failure - replayed, expired, wrong redirect, wrong PKCE, unknown - returns the SAME invalid_grant with the SAME description; the real reason goes to the log. A test asserts exactly one distinct description across four genuinely different failures, because saying which lets a caller retry the same code varying one parameter at a time. (2) LETTING THE REQUEST OVERRIDE THE GRANT. A refresh token presented with a different client_id or resource than its grant was issued for is refused - without that check, a leaked refresh token could be moved to whatever client an attacker controls. REVOKING ONE TOKEN REVOKES THE WHOLE GRANT, which is more than RFC 7009 requires and is what a seller means by 'disconnect'. Revoking an access token while its refresh token keeps minting new ones is a revocation that does not revoke. An unknown token still answers 200, per the RFC: reporting otherwise confirms which tokens are real to anyone willing to ask. Form-encoded, not JSON, because RFC 6749 requires it and the connector review checks for it. Cache-Control: no-store on every response including errors. STILL TO DO: /oauth/register (the deprecated DCR fallback) and Client ID Metadata Document fetching, both of which belong with the authorize endpoint in US-9121, plus flipping MCP_OAUTH_ENABLED once the consent screen exists. One test bug worth recording, because it read as an endpoint bug: the oracle test first seeded three codes up front, but setup() clears the previous code, so it exercised the last one three times - one of which was a fully valid request that correctly returned 200. Each case now seeds its own. [2026-08-18] sweep_oauth_expired is now CALLED, from handleDataRetentionCron alongside the connector audit sweep (see US-9113). It had no caller when 00620 shipped. [DONE 2026-08-19] The last two criteria landed: AC10 (an access token at /mcp) and AC9 (see and revoke connected apps). Migration 00620 is APPLIED - /health/ready reads expected 00620, applied 00620, match. Tests: src/tests/oauth-access_test.ts 12 passed, full edge suite 7660 passed / 0 failed, frontend tsc + eslint + ui:check clean. AC10: AN OAUTH TOKEN LANDS IN THE SAME TENANT CONTEXT AN API KEY DOES. lib/oauth-access.ts resolves it and mcp-auth fills the SAME Hono variables - userId, apiKeyId, apiKeyScopes, apiKeyPlan. Tools that behaved differently depending on how the caller signed in would be the worst kind of difference, one that only shows up for one class of user, so there is no second identity shape for anything downstream to learn about. apiKeyId CARRIES THE GRANT ID, deliberately. Every subject downstream keys off that variable - the audit row, the budget counter, the confirm-token binding - and a grant is the right unit: one seller's one connection to one client, revocable as a whole. So revoking a grant revokes its budget window and its audit trail's subject with it. FOUR CHECKS ON EVERY REQUEST, and the third is the one that matters: the token exists (looked up by HASH, never plaintext), it has not expired, its GRANT is not revoked, and the grant's resource is ours (RFC 8707). Without the revocation check, clicking disconnect would mean 'disconnect within an hour' and nobody would find out until it mattered. The audience check is the confused-deputy hole resource indicators exist to close; accepting a stranger's token because it parses is exactly how it stays open. EVERY FAILURE ANSWERS IDENTICALLY TO THE CALLER, with a test that asserts an unknown token and a revoked one produce the byte-identical result. Telling them apart tells someone holding a stolen token which it is. The reason goes to the log. THE ACCESS-TOKEN BRANCH RUNS BEFORE THE API-KEY PATH and only for the gta_ prefix, so a malformed API key still gets the API-key error rather than a confusing OAuth one. A guard pins that ordering by index. AC9: GET /api/oauth/connections and POST /api/oauth/connections/:id/revoke, rendered by src/components/api/connected-apps-panel.tsx on the API-keys page. Both were sabotage-verified - renaming gradethread_list_items fails the first, adding an argument fails the second. A third case guards the guards: the golden list must be at least ten entries and must match the registry length, because an assertion against an empty or truncated registry passes forever. TRANSPORT CONFORMANCE asserts the contract a client depends on rather than the implementation: server/discover reports every version we serve (and a client retrying from that list lands on one we accept), -32022 for an unsupported version, 404 + -32601 for an unknown method, -32020 for a mirrored header that disagrees with the body, -32700 with no id for malformed JSON, 405 for GET and DELETE, 202 with an empty body for a notification.
